system_overview: This specification models a simple key-value store exhibiting snapshot isolation. Concurrent transactions each work on a private snapshot of the store. If two concurrent transactions write to the same key, the one that commits later is rejected (write-write conflict detection). If they write to different keys, both succeed. The specification was contributed by Andrew Helwer.
actors_and_components: The system consists of a shared key-value store and a set of concurrent transaction processes identified by unique transaction IDs. Each transaction operates on a private snapshot of the store and can perform key additions, value updates, and key removals before attempting to commit or rolling back.
state_variables: The system tracks five pieces of state: (1) the shared data store mapping keys to values, (2) the set of currently open transactions, (3) each transaction's private snapshot of the store, (4) a per-transaction log of which keys have been written during the transaction, and (5) a per-transaction set of keys whose writes were missed (committed by other transactions after this transaction opened).
initial_state: The store maps all keys to a designated absence-of-value sentinel. No transactions are open. All transaction snapshots map all keys to the no-value sentinel. All write logs are empty sets. All missed-write sets are empty.
actions: There are six possible transitions: (1) Open transaction: a transaction not yet in the active set joins, and its snapshot is populated with the current store state. (2) Add: an open transaction sets a key that currently has no value in its snapshot to a new value, and records the key as written. (3) Update: an open transaction changes a key's value in its snapshot (the key must already have a value, and the new value must differ), recording the key as written. (4) Remove: an open transaction sets a key that currently has a value back to the no-value sentinel, recording the key as written. (5) Rollback: an open transaction is closed without merging changes; its snapshot, write log, and missed set are all reset to their initial empty states. (6) Close (commit): an open transaction whose written keys do not overlap with its missed keys merges its snapshot writes into the shared store. The transaction is removed from the active set, all other open transactions have the committing transaction's written keys added to their missed sets, and the committing transaction's snapshot and tracking state are reset.
safety_properties: Type invariant: the store maps keys to valid values, the transaction set is a valid subset of transaction IDs, snapshots are valid stores per transaction, write logs are sets of keys per transaction, and missed sets are sets of keys per transaction. Transaction lifecycle invariant: for any open transaction, if the store differs from the snapshot on a key that the transaction has not written, then that key must be in the missed set; for any inactive transaction, its snapshot must be all no-value sentinels and its write log and missed set must be empty.
model_bounds: The key set, value set, and transaction ID set are declared as constants. For model checking, typical small configurations use two to three keys, two to three values, and two to three transaction IDs.
additional_assumptions: The no-value sentinel is defined as a value chosen from outside the value set, ensuring it is distinguishable from any actual value. The specification does not include fairness assumptions or liveness properties; it focuses on safety verification of snapshot isolation's write-write conflict detection mechanism.
